Carl Wilhelm Scheele is a chemist. Carl Wilhelm Scheele (German: [ˈʃeːlə], Swedish: [ˈɧêːlɛ]; 9 December 1742 – 21 May 1786) was a German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist.
What is the atomic number of Oganesson?
Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
In what year was Pythagoras born?
Pythagoras: Pythagoras of Samos (Ancient Greek: Πυθαγόρας; c. 570 – c. 495 BC) was an ancient Ionian Greek philosopher, polymath, and the eponymous founder of Pythagoreanism.
In what year did Srinivasa Ramanujan die?
Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year was Silicon discovered?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
Which company manufactures Antonov An-124 Ruslan?
Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Aviastar-SP. The An-124 remains the largest military transport aircraft in service.
In which country is Dassault Rafale based?
Dassault Rafale: France. Dassault built a technology demonstrator that first flew in July 1986 as part of an eight-year flight-test programme, paving the way for approval of the project.
Who is credited with discovering Horologium?

Horologium (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. It was first described by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in 1756 and visualized by him as a clock with a pendulum and a second hand.
Who is credited with discovering Hubble's law?
Hubble's law: Georges Lemaître. The Friedmann equations showed the universe might be expanding, and presented the expansion speed if that were the case.
Who is credited with discovering Eris?
Eris (dwarf planet): Michael E. Brown. Eris (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
Hiding in coffee, fresh bread, and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is also what your liver makes when breaking down alcohol — and a prime culprit behind the morning-after hangover. What is it?
Acetaldehyde (IUPAC systematic name ethanal) is an organic chemical compound with the formula CH3CH=O.
This genus of more than 650 flowering succulent species includes a 'true' member cultivated worldwide as the standard source for a soothing pharmaceutical gel — what's the genus?
Aloe (also written Alo) is a genus containing over 650 species of flowering succulent plants.
Whether contracted through the skin, the lungs, or the gut, this Bacillus-driven infection can take up to two months to show symptoms — what is it?
Anthrax is an infection caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis or Bacillus cereus biovar anthracis.
This common vision condition occurs when the cornea or lens is slightly egg-shaped rather than spherical, causing blurred vision at any distance. What is it?
Astigmatism is a type of refractive error due to rotational asymmetry in the eye's refractive power.
This steel-gray, lightweight metal with atomic number 4 is found in gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, but within the cores of stars it gets destroyed as fast as it forms — what element is it?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
First described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado, this sauropod dinosaur's Greek name means arm lizard, a reference to its proportionately long front limbs — what genus is it?
Brachiosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 155.6 to 145.5 million years ago.
This group of diseases involves uncontrolled cell growth, includes over 100 types, and is responsible for about 33% of deaths when linked to tobacco and alcohol. What disease are we discussing?
Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.
Also known by the taxonomic synonym Epilobium, this hardy perennial in the willowherb family is native throughout the temperate north — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the willowherb family, Onagraceae.
This neurological disorder strikes one side of the head around the eye and temple, often at the very same hour each day for an 8-to-10-week stretch before vanishing for months — what condition is it?
Cluster headache is a neurological disorder characterized by episodes of severe headaches on one side of the head, typically around the eye and temple, lasting between 15 minutes to three hours.
Native to Europe and Western Asia, this birch-family shrub produces the round nuts sold commercially as hazelnuts — which species?
Corylus avellana is a species of flowering plant in the birch family Betulaceae.

This common cough suppressant found in cold medicine was combined with bupropion in 2022 to create a fast-acting antidepressant, despite belonging to the same chemical class as morphine — what drug is it?
Dextromethorphan is a cough suppressant used in many cough and cold medicines.
Named from Greek roots meaning 'to repeat' and 'speech,' this automatic repetition of another person's vocalizations is closely related to echopraxia, the repeating of movements. What is it called?
Echolalia is the repetition of vocalizations made by another person; when repeated by the same person, it is called palilalia.
This American physicist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a particle accelerator and later worked on uranium-isotope separation for the Manhattan Project. Who is he?
Ernest Lawrence (August 8, 1901 - August 27, 1958) was an American physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939 for his invention of the cyclotron.
This body part is a prominent, usually flexible digit found on the forelimbs of most four-limbed vertebrates — on the hind limbs, the equivalent shorter digits are instead called toes. What is it?
Finger is a prominent digit on the forelimbs of most tetrapod vertebrate animals, especially those with prehensile extremities (i.e.
First studied scientifically by an Augustinian friar experimenting with pea plants in 19th-century Brno, this branch of biology examines heredity and trait inheritance — which field?
Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
In this rapid-onset condition the immune system attacks the peripheral nerves, so weakness creeps up from the feet and hands — and about 15% of patients need a ventilator. What is it?
Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.

The reciprocal cross to the more common mule, this equine hybrid is the offspring of a male horse and a female donkey, differing from its counterpart in both physiology and temperament — what is it called?
Hinny is a domestic equine hybrid, the offspring of a male horse (a stallion) and a female donkey (a jenny).

This phenomenon describes how a system's state depends on its history, as when a magnet holds different moments depending on past field changes — it underlies memory in a hard disk drive. What is it called?
Hysteresis is the dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.

This American physicist worked on the Manhattan Project, then in 1949 proposed that — contrary to belief — not all atomic nuclei are spherical, an idea Aage Bohr later helped confirm. Who won a share of the 1975 Nobel for it?
James Rainwater (December 9, 1917 - May 31, 1986) was an American physicist who shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1975 for his part in determining the asymmetrical shapes of certain atomic nuclei.
Linked to a herpesvirus and immune suppression, this cancer causing purple skin lesions was already being described by Hippocrates in the 300s BC — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) is a type of cancer that can form masses on the skin, in lymph nodes, in the mouth, or in other organs.
Representing the Nemean Lion slain by Heracles as one of his twelve labors, this zodiac constellation sits between Cancer and Virgo — which constellation?
Leo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac, between Cancer, the Crab, to the west and Virgo, the Maiden, to the east.
Credited as the 'Father of Cinematography' for filming Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888, this French inventor mysteriously vanished in 1890 before cinema took off — who was he?

Louis Le Prince (28 August 1841 - disappeared 16 September 1890; declared dead 16 September 1897) was a French artist and the inventor of an early motion-picture camera, and director of Roundhay Garden Scene.
This Italian economist served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022 after previously heading the European Central Bank for eight years and the Bank of Italy before that — who is he?

Mario Draghi (born 3 September 1947) is an Italian politician, economist, academic, banker, statesman, and civil servant, who served as the prime minister of Italy from 13 February 2021 to 22 October 2022.
This medical condition is diagnosed when the erect length of the affected organ measures at least two and a half standard deviations below the average size for age — what condition is it?
Micropenis is an unusually small penis.
With shells that are elongated and wedge-shaped rather than round, these bivalves attach themselves to shorelines using threads nicknamed a "beard" — what are they?
Mussel is the common name used for members of several families of bivalve molluscs, from saltwater and freshwater habitats.
Catalyzed in nature by iron-bearing nitrogenase enzymes and famously partnered with legumes, this process turns molecular N2 into ammonia — what's it called?
Nitrogen fixation is a chemical process by which molecular dinitrogen (N2) is converted into ammonia (NH3).
All 14 species of this slim-bodied, dense-furred mammal are semiaquatic, and they're famous for playful antics like sliding into the water and juggling stones — what is it?
Otter are carnivorous mammals in the subfamily Lutrinae.
It comes in a G version for the needle and a V version for the mouth, and it owes its name to the very mould it's coaxed from — which medication?
Penicillin (PCN or PEN) are a group of beta-lactam antibiotics originally obtained from Penicillium moulds, principally P. chrysogenum.
This scientific term for a group of fin-footed, mostly marine mammals includes walruses, sea lions, fur seals, and true earless seals — 34 living species in all. What is the term?
Pinniped are a widely distributed and diverse clade of carnivorous, fin-footed, semiaquatic, mostly marine mammals.
Bloating, mood swings, breast tenderness and irritability that flare in the week or two before menstruation and fade once bleeding begins — what disruptive condition is this?
Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a disruptive set of emotional and physical symptoms that regularly occur in the one to two weeks before the start of each menstrual period.

Named for the ragged appearance of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants native mainly to North America has become an invasive nuisance in parts of Europe due to climate change — what plant is it?
Ragweed are flowering plants in the genus Ambrosia in the aster family, Asteraceae.

This long-term skin condition causes facial redness, pimples, and swelling, and can lead to a severely enlarged, reddened nose in extreme cases — its exact cause remains unknown — name this condition?
Rosacea is a long-term skin condition that typically affects the face.
About 950 species of these spiny, globe-shaped marine animals crawl the seabed on tube feet, found from tide pools down to 5,000 metres deep. What are they?
Sea urchin are the class Echinoidea within the echinoderms.
Pythons and boas of this limbless reptile group still carry a tiny pelvic girdle and vestigial leg-stubs near the cloaca, hinting at long-lost legs. What animal is this?
Snake are elongated legless reptiles of the suborder Serpentes.
A small Eurasian mustelid that turns brilliant white in winter, this animal's coat — known as ermine — once draped Catholic monarchs and the Infant Jesus of Prague — what is it?
Stoat (Mustela erminea), also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.
Named for a U.S. state where its discovery research was based, this synthetic element (symbol Ts) holds the second-highest atomic number of all and was the most recently discovered — what is it?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.

This parasite can infect nearly any warm-blooded animal, but can only sexually reproduce inside cats, and is famous for altering infected rodents' behavior to make them less afraid of feline predators — what parasite is it?
Toxoplasma gondii is a species of parasitic alveolate that causes toxoplasmosis.
Just 25 light-years away, this is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra and the fifth-brightest star in the entire night sky — what is it?
Vega is the brightest star in the northern constellation of Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
Chairman of the Polish People's Party since 2015 and a former Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, this physician-turned-politician ran for the Polish presidency in 2020 — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (born 10 August 1981) is a Polish physician and politician, who has served as the Deputy Prime Minister of Poland, and Minister of National Defence since 2023.
Unearthed in Montana by Jack Horner's team in 1987, this 20-foot horned dinosaur sported a bony neck-frill and lived roughly 75 million years ago — which species?
Achelousaurus: Genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from North America.
Often called the father of theoretical computer science, this Englishman gave us a famous 'machine' that formalized the very idea of computation — who was he?
Nicknamed 'whip-spiders' or 'tailless whip-scorpions,' these arachnids have no silk, no venom, and a name meaning 'blunt tail' — they grab with their pedipalps instead of biting — what order is this?
Amblypygi: Order of arachnids. The name "amblypygid" means "blunt tail", a reference to a lack of the flagellum that is otherwise seen in whip-scorpions.
Brought to Asia by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this tropical American tree produces a knobby, sweet fruit known as sugar apple or custard apple — what is this plant?
Annona squamosa: Species of tree. Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.
Its guanidino group serves as the biological precursor for nitric oxide production, and this amino acid earned the one-letter code 'R' purely for phonetic reasons — what is it?
Arginine: Amino acid. Arginine is the amino acid with the formula (H2N)(HN)CN(H)(CH2)3CH(NH2)CO2H.
This genus of early African hominins, which lived during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, is considered ancestral to the genus that includes modern humans — which genus?
Australopithecus: Genus of hominin ancestral to modern humans. The genera Homo (which includes modern humans), Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus evolved from some Australopithecus species.
With more than 2,000 species and petals but no sepals, this flowering plant genus originated in Africa and is popular as an ornamental houseplant in cooler climates — which genus?
Begonia: Genus of perennial flowering plants.
This medium-sized antelope of India and Nepal sports corkscrew horns up to 30 inches long and a striking two-tone coat, with white around the eyes set against black face stripes — which animal?
Blackbuck: Antelope native to India and Nepal. The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.
Nicknamed 'murderer's thumb' or 'stubbed thumb,' this genetic trait gives about 2% of people a short, rounded thumb linked to the HOXD13 gene — what is it?
Brachydactyly type D: Abnormal shortening of the distal part of the thumb.
Alongside HTML and JavaScript, which style sheet language handles the layout, colors, and fonts of a webpage — separating presentation from content?
CSS: Style sheet language. CSS is a cornerstone technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and JavaScript.

This group of heart-muscle diseases includes the 'broken heart syndrome' type and can lead to irregular heartbeats, fainting, or even sudden cardiac death — what's the general term for this condition?
Cardiomyopathy: Disease of the heart muscle. In dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and weaken.
Triggered by anything from a stroke to a bout of altitude sickness, this dangerous buildup of fluid inside the skull raises pressure on brain tissue and can cause seizures or worse — what is it?
Cerebral edema: Excess accumulation of fluid in the brain.

An essential nutrient your liver can only partly produce on its own, this compound builds phospholipids in cell membranes and helps make a neurotransmitter for muscle control, and occurs naturally in eggs, meat, and fish — which nutrient?
Choline: Chemical compound and essential nutrient. Choline is a cation with the chemical formula [(CH3)3NCH2CH2OH]+.

This ancient insect order traces back to the Late Jurassic, with chewing-mouthpart ancestors called "roachoids" scuttling around some 320 million years ago — yet only about 30 of its 4,600 species ever moved in with us. Which creature is it?
Cockroach: Insects of the order Blattodea.

Used in Chinese medicine for over 1,500 years, this genus of parasitic fungi infects insects and other arthropods, taking its name from Greek and Latin words meaning 'club' and 'head' — which genus is it?
Cordyceps: Genus of fungi. Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.
Sometimes called 'bipolar III,' this mood disorder involves cycling periods of mild depression and elevated mood that never reach the severity of full manic or depressive episodes — what is it?
Cyclothymia: Mental disorder. Cyclothymia differs from bipolar disorder in the fact that major depression and mania are not found.
Whether for an object, a process, or a system, this is the intentional concept or proposal created by a thinking agent, balancing purpose, aesthetics, and constraints — what single word names it?
Design: Plan for the construction of an object or system.
Brought to Australia as an infant, this geologist joined Shackleton's Nimrod Expedition and became a leading figure of the Heroic Age of Antarctic exploration — who is it?
Douglas Mawson: Australian geologist and explorer of the Antarctic (1882–1958)
This membrane-bound series of protein complexes shuttles electrons through redox reactions, building a proton gradient that ultimately powers the synthesis of ATP — what's it called?
Electron transport chain: Energy-producing metabolic pathway.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.

This branch of Islamic scholarship interprets the Quran and sunnah through jurist reasoning, producing fatwas — while sharia itself is seen as unchanging, this human field is considered fallible. What is it called?
Fiqh: Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, whereas sharia is considered immutable and infallible by Muslims, fiqh is considered fallible and changeable.
This cold-weather injury turns skin white or waxy-blue after tissue actually freezes, often preceded by a tingling, numb warning stage called frostnip — what is it?
Frostbite: Effect of low temperature on skin and other tissues.

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
This cluster of immune cells forms around bacteria, fungi, or foreign material the body can't otherwise clear away — what is it called?
Granuloma: Inflammatory aggregation of immune cells.

Coined by psychologist Edward Thorndike, this cognitive bias describes how a positive impression in one area, like someone's looks, skews our judgment of them in unrelated areas — what is this bias called?
Halo effect: Tendency for positive impressions to contaminate other evaluations.
Using only a triangle's three side lengths and their semiperimeter, this ancient geometric method computes the triangle's area — what is it known as?
Heron's formula: Triangle area in terms of side lengths.
A colorless, flammable liquid with an ammonia-like odor, this N2H4 compound foams polymer plastics, fills airbag gas generators, and serves as a storable spacecraft propellant. What is it?
Hydrazine: Colorless flammable liquid with an ammonia-like odor. It is a simple pnictogen hydride, and is a colourless flammable liquid with an ammonia-like odour.
Designed in 1967 to replace the An-12 and haul heavy machinery into remote, poorly served regions, this four-engine Soviet airlifter earned the NATO name 'Candid' — what is it?
Ilyushin Il-76: Russian heavy four-engined military transport jet aircraft.

This Mexican neurophysiologist studied shamanism, meditation, and telepathy through the scientific method, wrote more than 50 books on the subjects, and then vanished without a trace in December 1994 — who was he?
Jacobo Grinberg: Mexican pseudoscientist, neurophysiologist and psychologist.
Trained originally in mathematics at Cambridge, this English economist's Depression-era writings became the foundation for a whole school of macroeconomic thought bearing his name — who is he?
With an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters and a record of 5.85 meters, this snake is the world's longest venomous species, endemic to Asia. What is it?
King cobra: Group of venomous snakes from Asia.
Spread through the bite of sandflies, this parasitic disease can appear in cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral forms, the last marked by fever and an enlarged spleen — what is it called?
Leishmaniasis: Disease caused by parasites of the Leishmania type.

A domesticated South American camelid whose Quechua name the Spanish adopted, this herd animal can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles and learns simple tasks after a few tries — what is it?
Llama: Species of wooly domesticated mammal.
Found from Gibraltar to across Asia, these Old World monkeys live in troops centered on dominant matriarchs, and one Malaysian species eats about 70 rats a year — what are they?
Macaque: Genus of Old World monkeys. The macaques constitute a genus (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
Kangaroos, koalas, and wombats all belong to this mammal group whose young are born undeveloped and finish developing in their mother's pouch — what group is it?
Marsupial: Infraclass of mammals in the clade Metatheria.
The only operational rocket-powered fighter ever fielded, this WWII German interceptor became the first piloted aircraft to exceed 1,000 km/h in level flight — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Me 163 Komet: German rocket-powered interceptor. The Messerschmitt Me 163 Komet is a rocket-powered interceptor aircraft primarily designed and produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Messerschmitt.

This Serbian polymath — mathematician, astronomer, civil engineer — explained Earth's long-term climate swings by tracking our planet's shifting position relative to the Sun, a theory of cycles that now bears his name. Who was he?
Milutin Milanković: Serbian scientist and professor (1879–1958)
Produced by glands throughout the body's linings — including the respiratory, digestive, and urogenital tracts — which slippery substance traps and destroys harmful bacteria and viruses?
Mucus: Secretion produced by mucous membranes.

Nicknamed the 'flesh-eating disease' even though the bacteria don't actually consume tissue — they release toxins that kill it instead — this fast-spreading infection often enters through a cut or burn. What condition is it?
Necrotizing fasciitis: Infection that results in the death of the body's soft tissue.
This carnivorous freshwater fish, found widely across cold waters worldwide, has a current all-tackle world record of 25 kg, caught in Germany in 1986 — what species is it?
Northern pike: Species of fish. The northern pike (Esox lucius), also known as jack, northern or simply pike, is a species of carnivorous fish of the genus Esox (pikes).

Sitting between tissue and a full body system in life's hierarchy, this general term describes a structural unit built from functional tissue (parenchyma) plus supportive tissue (stroma), as seen in the intestinal wall — what is such a unit called?
Organ (biology): Collection of tissues with similar functions.
Which of these is a recognised non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease?
Loss of the sense of smell
A reduced sense of smell often appears years before the tremor and slowness that people associate with the disease, alongside sleep disturbance and autonomic problems.

Caused by a lack of intrinsic factor — often from an autoimmune attack on the stomach — this vitamin B12 deficiency disorder brings gradual fatigue, a smooth red tongue, and numbness in the hands and feet — which condition?
Pernicious anemia: Lack of red blood cells due to vitamin B12 deficiency.
Evergreen conifers of the genus Pinus, these trees grow their needle leaves in bunches of two to five and yield both the nuts used in pesto and the resin that flavors retsina wine?
Pine: Genus of coniferous trees. A pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.
Better known in the kitchen as cream of tartar, this winemaking byproduct helps stabilize egg whites for fluffier meringues — what compound is it?
Potassium bitartrate: Chemical salt used in cooking as cream of tartar.
Crossing the line between the natural and social sciences, this discipline scientifically studies the mind and behavior — both conscious and unconscious — in humans and other animals. What is it?
Psychology: Study of mental functions and behaviors.
This genus of roughly 1,750 flowering plant species includes the buttercups, spearworts, and water crowfoots — which genus?
Ranunculus: Genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family.
Its seeds yield castor oil but also harbor a highly potent toxin — which plant genus, better known for producing the castor bean?
Ricinus: Monotypic genus of plant in the spurge family.
Belonging to the order Urodela and reaching their greatest diversity in the Appalachian Mountains, these tailed, lizard-shaped amphibians never have more than four front toes — what are they?
Salamander: Order of amphibians. All ten extant salamander families are grouped together under the order Urodela, the sole surviving order from the group Caudata.
Named from Greek words meaning 'horse' and 'sea monster,' this small bony fish sports an upright posture, a curled tail, and bony armor plating — which creature is it?
Blurring the line between a single creature and a colony, this cnidarian is actually made of specialized zooids from one fertilized egg working together to float, feed and jet-propel — what is it?
Siphonophore: Order of colonial hydrozoans with differentiated zooids.
With over 60 types found throughout the human body, this ring-shaped muscle keeps a bodily passage closed until it relaxes to let something through — what is it called?
Sphincter: Circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice.

This speech disorder involves involuntary repetitions and prolongations of sounds or words, affects roughly 1% of the world's population, and is unrelated to a person's ability to structure their thoughts — what's it called?
Stuttering: Speech disorder. Persistent stuttering into adulthood often leads to outcomes detrimental to overall mental health, such as social isolation and suicidal thoughts.
Pig-shaped with a short, flexible snout, this odd-toed ungulate mammal lives in the jungles of South and Central America and Southeast Asia, alongside equine and rhino relatives — which animal?
This body region between the hip and the knee contains a single bone — the femur — that forms a ball-and-socket joint above and a hinge joint below. What is it?
Thigh: Body part between pelvis and knee; upper leg.
Also known as the windpipe, this cartilaginous tube linking the throat to the lungs is reinforced by horseshoe-shaped rings of cartilage — what is it?
Trachea: Cartilaginous tube. The trachea extends from the larynx and branches into the two primary bronchi.
Carrying the placeholder symbol Ubb, this hypothetical element 122 is expected to sit within the 'island of stability' — what is its systematic IUPAC name?
Unbibium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 122 (Ubb)

Most animals make their own, but humans, guinea pigs, and some bats must eat it because a synthesis-enzyme gene is broken; this citrus nutrient builds collagen and acts as an antioxidant — what is it?
Vitamin C: Essential nutrient found in citrus fruits and other foods.
Ranging from a few meters for Bluetooth to millions of kilometers for deep-space signals, this method of sending information relies on radio waves instead of cables -- what is it called?
Wireless: Transfer of information or power that does not require the use of physical wires.
Tellurium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for tellurium is Te. Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
Darmstadtium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for darmstadtium is Ds. Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.

In what year was Diane Keaton born?
Diane Keaton (née Hall; January 5, 1946 – October 11, 2025) was an American actress.
In what year was Jeremy Allen White born?
Jeremy Allen White (born February 17, 1991) is an American actor.
In what year was Hayden Panettiere born?
Hayden Panettiere: Hayden Lesley Panettiere ( PAN-ə-tee-AIR; born August 21, 1989) is an American actress.
In what year was Gene Wilder born?
Gene Wilder (born Jerome Silberman; June 11, 1933 – August 29, 2016) was an American actor, author, comedian, writer and filmmaker.
In what year was Josh Hutcherson born?
Josh Hutcherson: Joshua Ryan Hutcherson (born October 12, 1992) is an American actor.
In what year was Juno Temple born?
Juno Temple (born 21 July 1989) is an English actress.
In what year was Ralph Fiennes born?
Ralph Fiennes: Ralph Nathaniel Twisleton-Wykeham-Fiennes (born 22 December 1962) is an English actor and director.
In what year was J. K. Rowling born?
